assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks (magic-wavelength trapping of neutral atoms) are a clear, original invention that gave the most accurate measurements ever made, with direct consequences for redefining the second, tests of fundamental constants and relativistic geodesy. The idea, its realization and its statistical-metrology payoff (many atoms, low quantum projection noise) are crisp and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated early Sr clocks; Jun Ye brought it to the highest accuracy and stability and to many-body-aware clocks. A two-person prize is a clean configuration; some uncertainty about the roles of other Sr/Yb groups and of frequency-comb and cold-atom precursors.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by many groups worldwide at the 1e-18 level; the technology is mature and international redefinition of the second is in discussion. Recognition is timely, with no sign of interpretive instability.
uncertainties: Contributions of other lattice-clock groups (for example Yb and Hg communities) and of earlier ion-clock and comb work could be argued as part of the credit.
I rely on recalled accuracy figures and the status of the redefinition of the second, not verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cold atoms in optical lattices turned strongly correlated many-body models (Hubbard, Mott transition, superfluid-insulator physics) into controllable laboratory systems. The conceptual originality lies in quantum simulation of lattice models; the impact reaches condensed-matter, statistical and quantum-information physics.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch and others) supplied the Hubbard-model proposal, Greiner and Bloch the decisive 2002 Mott-insulator realization and subsequent quantum-gas microscopes, and Esslinger the fermionic Hubbard and transport work. A four-name field cannot fit in three, so Esslinger is the main exclusion and is arguable; Zoller's credit also overlaps with other candidates.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally confirmed over two decades by multiple independent groups; benchmarks against numerics now exist, though a decisive solution of an open problem such as the doped Hubbard model is still pending.
uncertainties: Choice of three among four credited names is a judgment call, and Esslinger's claim is comparable.
Overlap with the Cirac-Zoller candidates raises the question of how to allocate Zoller's recognition.
Whether the field's best discoveries are simulation results or the method itself remains debatable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Active matter statistics is a genuinely new branch of nonequilibrium statistical physics: the Vicsek model, the Toner-Tu hydrodynamic theory (long-range order in 2D flocks, anomalous fluctuations) and the Ramaswamy hydrodynamics of active suspensions. It connects to my own fields of stochastic dynamics, biological collectives and complex systems and has shaped a very large literature.
assessment.attribution: Vicsek introduced the minimal flocking model, Toner and Tu derived the continuum theory with exact scaling results, and Ramaswamy contributed the hydrodynamics of active fluids and orientational order; the credit set matches the conceptual founders well, though others (for example Marchetti, Cates, Yeomans) have strong claims on later developments.
assessment.maturity: Predictions such as giant number fluctuations and flocking phases have experimental support in vibrated granular matter, bacterial suspensions and colloids, but quantitative confirmation of the Toner-Tu exponents is partial. The theory is mature but the experimental verification of its sharpest claims is still ongoing.
uncertainties: Quantitative experimental confirmation of the 2D flocking exponents is limited.
Cleanly separating the foundational contribution from the broader active-matter community is difficult.
As a statistical physicist working near this field I should discount possible familiarity bias.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED created a strong-coupling, engineerable light-matter platform in superconducting circuits, with the transmon, dispersive readout and bosonic encodings as downstream achievements. It is a foundational architecture for solid-state quantum technology, importantly different from the macroscopic quantum tunnelling work already recognized in 2025 (as I recall).
assessment.attribution: Blais, Girvin, Schoelkopf and collaborators proposed and demonstrated circuit QED in 2004; Schoelkopf's group led the experiments and transmon, Blais and Girvin the theory. The set is plausible, but the field also has other contributors (for example Nakamura, Wallraff, Devoret as an experimental co-leader) so credit is not fully settled.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups; the platform underpins commercial quantum processors. The scientific interpretation is stable, but timing relative to the 2025 prize may make a second superconducting-circuit award appear soon.
uncertainties: Whether a second superconducting-circuit award shortly after 2025 is appropriate.
Wallraff and Nakamura, and Devoret's overlapping role, complicate attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator, with experimental discovery in HgTe wells, opened a whole class of topological materials with robust boundary states; a conceptual change comparable to the quantum Hall era.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the original Z2 proposal; Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental realization (with Zhang's theory on HgTe, which is outside the supplied credit). Allocation is reasonably clean among the supplied names, but the absence of Bernevig, Zhang and Hasan-type 3D discoveries from this entry makes it incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Many independent confirmations by transport and ARPES across materials; the field is mature and timely, although the practical impact is still limited.
uncertainties: Credit for the HgTe prediction and 3D topological insulators lies outside the named three.
Overlap with the other topological candidate (B049) in credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Moire flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a new tunable platform for strongly correlated physics and are widely seen as a major discovery of the last decade.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat band at the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group demonstrated correlated states and superconductivity. The theory-experiment pairing is clean, though Cao as first author and other experimental groups complicate the experimental side.
assessment.maturity: Replicated widely, but the origin of superconductivity and the ground states remain actively debated; recognition is somewhat early.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity is unsettled.
Premature relative to the stability of the interpretation.
Young researchers' roles are not captured by the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The jamming picture of the transition from fluid to rigid disordered matter links granular matter, glasses and foams through marginal stability and critical scaling. It is statistically deep and conceptually unifying, though not itself a decisive, simple discovery.
assessment.attribution: Liu and Nagel proposed the jamming phase diagram; Wyart and collaborators developed marginal stability and isostaticity arguments, so a two-person prize omits an important theoretical contributor, while three may seem diffuse. O'Hern, Silbert and others also contributed to the numerics.
assessment.maturity: Simulations and some experiments support the critical behavior, but the relevance to real glasses and the universality class remain debated, so recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: Applicability to thermal glasses is contested.
Allocation among Liu, Nagel and Wyart is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-precision CMB anisotropy mapping (WMAP and associated ground and balloon experiments) fixed the parameters of the standard cosmological model, a lasting empirical foundation. The 2006 prize to COBE already recognized the first anisotropies, so the new element is the precision measurement.
assessment.attribution: WMAP's leadership (Bennett as PI, Page and Spergel in instrument and analysis) is a plausible trio, though Planck (Puget), BOOMERanG and others contributed; credit would be somewhat arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by Planck and ground experiments; mature and stable interpretation. Possible redundancy with the earlier prize reduces the novelty of a new award.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2006 prize and large-collaboration credit make it hard to pick a three-person set.
Planck's role is relevant but represented by only one credited name.
